known_misconfigurations.summary: The dev bundle sets profile cpu with IBEX_EMBEDDING_DIM=1024, so the deterministic stub emits 1024-dimension vectors under the 384-dimension model id all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Writes pass the embedding_dim = 1024 check while the recorded model name describes a model that never runs.

ibex.worker.embedding.noop is still the only embedding task: there is no backfill task and no generation column, so switching an embedding model requires the manual, resumable-by-rerun procedure in engineering/runbooks/re-embed.md. The model fence shipped, but a fence is not a re-embed.

The write path records the configured identity -- IBEX_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_MODEL, plus @<revision> when IBEX_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_MODEL_REVISION is set -- rather than the model the embedder reports: write/factory.py still discards result.model_id, and nothing compares the configured identity with the embedder's /v1/models before a write. A deployment whose embedder serves a different model, or the same id at different weights without the revision variable set, records an identity that does not describe the vector.

SEARCH_SQL and SearchRequest.embedding_model now carry a model fence, but it is off by default and evaluated as a post-filter over the HNSW candidate set, so a fenced search can lose recall while two generations share one column; the full-text channel is not fenced at all. The durable fix is one index per live generation during a re-embed, not a predicate.

The embedding cache digest now covers model_id, dimensions and the weights revision, but the revision is hashed only when IBEX_EMBEDDING_MODEL_REVISION is set; leaving it unset keeps the pre-revision byte layout for compatibility, so two deployments that differ only in weights still share digests. Pinning --revision obliges the operator to set the variable, and nothing enforces that pairing.
